A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPRT study and contain readable main text and Appendices A–G. Equations, tables, figures, and experiments can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, human annotation validation, counterfactual experiments, and supervised fine-tuning results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark in Table 3 and additional fine-tuning comparisons in appendix Table 5.

M1.justification: The four-level taxonomy, attribute assignment, embedding-based boundary extraction, lexicographic scoring, prompting procedures, and LoRA fine-tuning remain unchanged. The added adversary description does not introduce a new computational step.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VISPR-derived data for privacy-attribute and severity assessment, human validation, and counterfactual facial-anonymization scenarios. No additional dataset, domain, or evaluated task is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same eight VLMs under all three prompting strategies. The additional Qwen3-VL and Llama SFT comparisons also remain identical; v1 Table 6 becomes v2 Table 5.

E3.justification: The 6,736-image evaluation set, 3,630-image SFT set, annotation rules, metrics, inference settings, and training budgets are unchanged. Both retain the 65-image human validation study and 100-image counterfactual experiment.

E4.justification: Both retain the prompting comparisons, counterfactual analysis, SFT model-family and size comparisons, confusion matrices, and score distributions. Removing the counterfactual subsection number does not remove or revise its analysis.

E5.justification: Human-agreement statistics and estimation procedures are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or specified significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the corresponding main and appendix performance tables match, and all 16 figure images are identical. For example, taxonomy-guided Gemini retains Spearman 0.872, while Qwen3-VL 8B + SFT retains Spearman 0.762 and MAE 0.140.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an adversary definition (A, C, G), representing auxiliary information, capabilities, and goals, and relates severity levels to required auxiliary information. The scoring equations and Appendix A properties and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The claims about CPRT, continuous scoring, the 6.7K-image benchmark, intermediate-risk failures, and deployable 8B fine-tuning remain. Removing 'ground-truth' from selected passages does not change the defined scoring targets or contribution scope.

C2.justification: The new Section 3.2 paragraph explicitly interprets severity through adversary resources and goals, including the assertion that L4 cannot achieve those goals under realistic conditions. Existing result interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Unlike v1, v2's abstract states that the dataset and models are publicly available and supplies a Hugging Face collection link. This adds access information; hardware, hyperparameters, processing details, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 38 cited works and research positioning. Reference 31 changes from preprint metadata to a CVPR Workshops publication entry for the same work.

P1.justification: v2 adds keywords and funding acknowledgments, shortens selected wording, and adjusts headings and cross-references. The narrative and organization of the main sections and Appendices A–G remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively retypeset with a narrower text area, different typography, running headers, and resized or repositioned figures and tables. The legal mapping becomes unnumbered, and annotation/results Tables 5/6 become 4/5. Figure content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit adversary assumptions in Section 3.2 and newly supplied dataset/model access information modestly improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited: experiments and proofs remain unchanged, and the new layout compresses some tables.
